text:
marta: Running a quick nsys compare between `main` and the `v2026-03` tag — seeing ~1.8x regression in attention_forward kernel time. Timeline attached. Anyone else noticing this? :eyes:
kevin: Which commit did you land on? any obvious changes to kernel selector or batching?
sasha: Can you paste the nsys summary / the small flame snippet? even a screenshot link helps.
marta: Pasting condensed output from the two runs:
```
# nsys summary (attention_forward hot kernel)
# prev-tag (v2026-03): 6.8 ms (median)
# main @ a34c7b9: 12.3 ms (median)
# increase mainly in kernel launch count and per-launch overhead
```
build-bot: bisect-run started on commit range a12..a34 — job id: bisect-1769504321 — updates in #eng-runtime when done.
ryan: Possible suspects: batching heuristic change that splits requests more aggressively, or KV cache path that forces repeated KV uploads. Both would increase small kernel launches.
marta: Perfetto timeline shows a repeating pattern: nvtx ranges marking `token_step` with many tiny kernels between them. Looks like we lost some batching aggregation. Link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1769504321 (uploaded)
kevin: I recall a change in `batch_split_threshold` in a34c7b9. For short sequences it switches to a fallback loop instead of single fused kernel. That could explain more launches and float path fallback.
sasha: Can you run nsys with `--trace=cuda,kern,nvtx` and export sqlite? I'll grep kernel durations and launch counts. Command I use:
```
nsys profile --output=/tmp/p.1 --trace=cuda,kern,nvtx --quiet --sample=none ./inference_bench --model M
nsys export --output=/tmp/p.1.sqlite /tmp/p.1.nsys-rep
```
marta: Uploaded sqlite to `//shared/profiles/1769504321_ns.sqlite` and a grep I ran shows many `attention_forward` entries ~0.2-0.4 ms each instead of fewer ~6-12ms consolidated ones.
ryan: That matches a batching split bug. Also check KV cache nvtx markers — if every token sequence triggers `kv_upload` that's a big perf win/loss.
marta: I grep'd nvtx "kv_upload": previous run had 1 per request, new run has 1 per token_step chunk.
kevin: If bisect finishes, we'll know which commit added the changed heuristic. If it's the `batch_split_threshold` tweak we can try reverting the logic or increasing the threshold.
build-bot: bisect update: narrowed to single commit b3f9f1 (tested 8 candidates) — flagged as regression-causer.
sasha: Nice. Can someone check diff around b3f9f1 for `batching::should_split` & `kernel_selector` fallback conditions?
kevin: I looked — b3f9f1 introduced an early-exit path that forces sequence <8 to use the per-token loop to avoid OOM in rare cases. It didn't account for KV caching which makes the loop expensive.
ryan: Proposed patch: add KV-aware guard and aggregate small sequences if KV hits are high. Quick change attached in PR draft.
marta: Rebuilt with revert of the early-exit and re-ran nsys: attention_forward median back to 6.9 ms, launch count down 8x. Bisect confirmed b3f9f1.
kevin: Great delta. Please upload perfetto & nsys side-by-side, and add a unit/integration test that runs short sequences with KV cache enabled so we don't regress again.
sasha: I'll add a perf regression check doc and a tiny CI job that runs the nsys sampling for that path (nightly only).
marta: Filing an internal ticket: INF-1284 with traces attached, bisect results, proposed patch. Assigning to kevin & ryan.
ryan: I'll open the PR with the KV-aware aggregation fix and CI test. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
kevin: Heads-up: we should also add telemetry counters for per-request kernel_launch_count and kv_uploads so ops can alert on this class of regression automatically.
marta: Agreed — adding to roadmap for Optimize/Observability.
build-bot: Note: bisect job completed in ~22m. Logs at //ci/bisect/1769504321.log
